source: The official AR app page lists screws, Allen keys and screwdrivers among the items shown in its animations (https://www.iafsm.in/index.php/component/sppagebuilder/?view=page&id=59). Tool sizes are not published; the fastener-to-tool pairing below is inferred from the screw heads in the CAD model.

tools.name: Allen (hex) key set
tools.use: Insert the short arm fully into the screw socket and turn with the long arm for torque. Use the ball end only for reaching angled screws, not for final tightening.
tools.reason: The frame, plates, brackets and station mounts are joined with socket-head screws, which take high torque without slipping and fit in tight spaces.
safety: Use the exact size — a loose key rounds the socket.
Make sure the key is fully seated before applying force.
Isolate power before working near the drive train or stations.
Tighten in a cross pattern so plates seat evenly.

tools.name: Phillips screwdriver
tools.use: Match the tip size to the screw, keep the shaft in line with the screw and push firmly while turning.
tools.reason: Cross-head screws appear on the servo drive mounting.
safety: Switch off and isolate the supply before touching electrical equipment.
Wrong tip sizes cam out and damage the screw head.
Hold the workpiece, not the area in front of the tip.

tools.name: Flat-blade (terminal) screwdriver
tools.purpose: Tightens terminal screws and releases DIN-rail clips.
tools.use: Use a narrow insulated blade for terminal screws. To remove a module, lever the DIN clip down at the bottom of the module and tilt it off the rail.
tools.reason: Terminal blocks, the power supply, DIN modules and the circuit breaker are wired with screw terminals and held by DIN-rail clips.
safety: Use an insulated (VDE) screwdriver for electrical terminals.
Never work on terminals while the circuit is live; switch off the circuit breaker and verify.
Do not overtighten small terminal screws.
